instructions.task: Tag the final persuader message ('Persuader message to tag') in a chat where the persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate part of their task payment to Save the Children. Pick the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses.
notes: Use the earlier chat only as context (its lines may be out of order).
Judge what the tagged message itself does.

criteria.greeting: Opening pleasantries at the start of the chat: hello, hi, how are you, I'm good how are you, nice to meet you.
criteria.closing: Goodbyes and closing wishes: have a great night, enjoy your day, bye.

agree_or_react.definition: A genuine reaction to or agreement with an opinion, feeling or fact the persuadee just shared.
examples: I agree 100%
That's true
ok, I understand that
Absolutely.
Wow that is so good to hear
I understand financial strain

filler.definition: A bare filler or minimal token with no real reaction.
examples: Ok...
Fine...
Yeah.
yes, indeed.
Indeed.

answer_question.definition: Answers a question the persuadee asked, when the answer is not a fact about Save the Children.
examples: Yes, I'm familiar with them
I have.
I am doing well thank you.

criteria.confirm_or_push_amount: Checks or confirms a donation figure the persuadee mentioned ('Half of 1 dollar?', 'so that's 20 cents, right?'), or pushes for a larger amount than offered.
criteria.task_remark: Remarks about the chat task / HIT / survey itself (number of chats needed, payment for the HIT, how the task works) that are not about how the donation works.

me_too.definition: The persuader says they feel or did the same as the persuadee, or shares their own matching reaction, rather than agreeing with a point the persuadee made.
examples: Me too!
Yes, I was really surprised too.
neither do i!
I know I have.

praise_user.definition: Compliments the persuadee, or a positive exclamation right after the persuadee commits to donating or states an amount.
examples: People like you make the world better.
That's awesome and generous!
you are a very kind person
Great! (after the persuadee says they will donate)

criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee (thank you, thanks so much).
criteria.off_task: Casual chit-chat unrelated to the charity, donating or the task: places, weather, hobbies, the persuader's own life unrelated to children or giving.

personal_inquiry.definition: Asks about the persuadee's own life, family or personal habits, including their own donation history.
examples: Do you have children?
Where are you from?
Do you usually give to charities?
Have you ever donated to them?

task_inquiry.definition: Asks the persuadee's opinion or feelings about the cause, children's issues, or donating.
examples: Is this something that you care about?
What do you think about children in war zones?
Have you heard of children getting separated at the border?

source_inquiry.definition: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of Save the Children, or what they know about it.
examples: Are you familiar with Save the Children?
Have you heard of them?

org_facts.definition: Facts or praise about Save the Children itself: what it is, what it does, where it works, its history and founder, its ratings and reputation, how funds are spent, its website or URL. Also when answering the persuadee's question about the charity, and when a suffering fact is tied to the charity acting on it.
examples: It is an international charity that helps children in need.
86% of funds go to program services.
It's one of the top rated charities.
The web address is URL

donation_effect_reasoning.definition: Reasoning that donating has an effect, or moral reasoning about why one should give (not about small amounts).
examples: Donations make a huge difference in the lives of these kids.
They are only able to help when people donate.
Charity is important and everyone deserves a fighting chance.

suffering_emotion.definition: Facts, statistics or stories about children's suffering (deaths, war, hunger, disease), stories of a child the charity helped, the persuader's feelings about the children, or anything that evokes sadness, guilt, sympathy or hope.
examples: Did you know 5.6 million children die every year from preventable causes?
1000 children have been killed in Syria.
It makes me so sad that children lack clean water.
Imagine how happy the children will be.

criteria.personal_story: A narrative of the persuader's own experience that is not about children's suffering or the persuader's giving (rare).

self_modeling.definition: The persuader states their own past, habitual or intended donation, or offers to donate/match.
examples: I donate to them every year myself.
I will donate the same amount you decide.
I gave what was given to me.

small_amount.definition: Frames the request as small and painless: every little bit helps, donate a little, even a few cents, an amount you won't miss.
examples: Every little bit helps.
Believe it or not, 10 cents makes a difference!
$2 you won't miss.

donation_procedure.definition: How the donation works: it is deducted from the task payment, the research team sends it, the allowed range ($0 to full payment), any amount is acceptable, donate what you can, or a neutral suggestion of an amount.
examples: Your donation will be directly deducted from your task payment.
You can choose any amount from $0 to $2.
May I suggest $.50 or even $1 if you are able?
you can help by donating what you can

propose_donation.definition: Asks, invites or urges the persuadee to donate, without asking for a specific amount.
examples: Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?
Would you consider donating?
We should donate to them!

ask_amount.definition: Open question about how much the persuadee will donate.
examples: How much would you like to give?
What amount would you feel comfortable donating?

criteria.check_in: A generic check-in or offer of help that is not about donating or the charity: Does that sound ok to you? Is there any information I could provide?
criteria.other_misc: Anything else that fits none of the above.
